For more than 125 years, Goodyear has developed tire technologies and solutions to give people the confidence to go further and faster. It’s Goodyear’s spirit of innovation that keeps vehicles on roads of every surface, around racetracks, in the air and even on the moon.
Goodyear’s innovative tires have been industry leaders for more than 125 years. The company introduced the first “all-weather” tire, sent tires to the moon and claims the winningest racing tires around the world. Throughout its history, Goodyear has enhanced mobility from streets and highways to farms and work sites and even in the skies. It has developed tires that improve traction on slippery roads, maximize fuel economy and continue to run even when flat.
Goodyear’s scientists, engineers and researchers have continually discovered new solutions and opportunities for changing mobility needs. For example, polymer research led to the development of synthetic rubber for use in tires and beyond. Material science unearthed new components to enhance performance and durability. And new technology was applied to tire design and enabled virtual tire testing.

Goodyear is more than a tire manufacturer. Since its founding, Goodyear has evolved to become a technology-driven company that enables mobility. Along the way, it also has innovated its business models, expanded its manufacturing and sales and even became the first tire brand to sell directly to consumers online. More breakthroughs, such as mobile tire installation, are setting the pace for the industry for the next 125 years.

entityDescription:
The Institute of Microbiology of the CAS represents the largest scientific body extensively exploring life cycles, molecular mechanisms and regulatory systems of various microorganisms such as bacteria, yeast, fungi and algae) as well as mammalian cell lines with respect to basic research questions as well as their prospective practical exploitation in medicine and industry.
The main research interests of our Institute represent cellular and molecular microbiology, genetics and physiology of microorganisms and their resistance to antibiotics, production of microbial metabolites and their biotransformation, and grading up production strains by genetic modifications etc.
Another main research direction is embodied by soil ecology, ecotoxicology and microbial degradation of organic pollutants in the natural environment. An immunological section of the Institute then studies the importance of microorganisms in phylogenetic and ontogenetic acquisition of immunity as well as during the onset of autoimmune diseases and, last but not least, it is also focused on immunotherapies of oncogenic diseases.
Institute of Microbiology of the CAS has an internationally recognized collection of basidiomycetes and its own biotechnological unit, which is mainly used to monitor microbiological and biotechnological processes at a semi-operational scale.
IM CAS has three satellite working units outside of Prague; the first of which is in Trebon (research on phototrophic microorganisms) the second is in Novy Hradek (gnotobiology) and third is in Nove Hrady (Center for Nanobiology and Structural Biology).
Despite the fact that the Institute of Microbiology of the CAS is preferentially focused on the basic research, many of its outputs find or will find practical use in pharmaceutical as well as biotechnological industry as documented by a genuine interest of a number of private companies in our scientific work.

entityDescription:
The Spanish National Cancer Research Centre (CNIO) was founded in 1998 within the Instituto de Salud Carlos III (ISCiii). The CNIO operates as a public foundation, governed by its Board of Trustees. It conducts research of excellence in oncology, translates scientific knowledge into clinical practice, and transfers the technology developed at the CNIO to the productive sector.
Employing more than 500 researchers, our scientific activities are undertaken by 28 Groups, 18 Core Units and 3 Sections. The Groups are organized in a Basic Research Area (Molecular Oncology and Structural Biology Programmes) and a Patient-Oriented Research Area (Human Cancer Genetics and Clinical Research Programmes). Also, there are two Programmes under the Innovation Direction, the Biotechnology Programme, providing scientific and technological support, and the Experimental Therapeutics Programme, focused on early drug discovery.
The CNIO is recognised as one of the top leading Cancer Research Institutes worldwide, and its scientific contributions are published in top journals. During the last five years, the CNIO has increased its scientific productivity, with 395 publications in journals with impact factor higher than 10 (vs. 330 in the period 2014-2018). According to the latest SCImago Report, the CNIO occupies the 8th position among cancer-focused research centres worldwide, and the 3rd in Europe. In the ranking of Nature Index 2024, the CNIO holds the 9th position worldwide, the 2nd in Europe, across cancer research centres.

entityDescription:
Computer vision (CV) is a discipline that focuses on developing techniques through which computers can perceive and interpret the content of digital images. CV is used in many industrial applications for quality control or anomaly detection, and increasingly, CV systems are based on artificial intelligence (AI) for image analysis. In AI developments, data is the most crucial and valuable pillar. In the real world, collecting accurate and high-quality data is complex, expensive, and time-consuming. A certain portion of the labelled data will contain inaccuracies due to human interaction in the annotation process. Additionally, for rare defects / anomalies, the difficulty of collecting a sufficient number of images is even greater, especially in space applications where products or applications are produced in very small batches. 
With our product, Synigen, the customer can generate accurate, high-quality, automatically annotated, and labelled realistic synthetic images of a 3D object or scene with the automatic integration of anomalies or defects on the chosen objects. The intuitive graphical interface allows the user to create large datasets of a product containing defects/anomalies even before the actual production begins. This dataset can be used as input for training an AI model that can be used in any computer vision task. The advantages compared to real data are: 
- Speed: there is no need to wait for the "real-world" setup to capture a sufficient number of images suitable for anomaly detection, even for rarely occurring anomalies. 
- Accuracy: our images are automatically labeled and annotated, eliminating biases/errors introduced by human interaction in the process. 
- Flexibility: the models can be easily updated or modified without costly impact. 
- Cost: compared to "real-world" images, our synthetic images cost only a fraction.
With our approach, non-software people can create the necessary data, leaving the software/machine learning engineers use their skills and talent to other complicated tasks. 
A CV based on our solution would be a perfect add-on for: 
• automated anomaly inspection (defects, wrong assembly, PCB…) or for self-diagnostics of systems 
• automated object recognition for spatial situational awareness (debris or adversarial entities) or for part detection 
 
Besides the software, our company is specialized in the development of the needed hardware, with or without robots, for capturing the needed anomalies in an image as well as doing inference on these images allowing self-diagnostics or situational awareness.
The existing NDT (non-destructive testing) for major aerospace suppliers (materials, engine parts, bolts…) can benefit of our solution. In a further future, automatically conditioned and functioning farms and systems will be necessary in long distance travelling (to Mars) or missions on the surface of Mars / Moon. Therefore, an AI system helping the detection of anomalies will be inevitable.
